We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-1.54<Z<1.54).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/af13b1b1ef963dc2a922eab8b213015bd5af23b28fbf907fe4b7e5226a8768f4.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.54<Z<1.54) & =P(Z<1.54)-P(Z\le -1.54) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.54)-P(Z\le -1.54) \\  & =Φ(1.54)-Φ(-1.54)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-1.54)=0.0618,
$$

but we are not given $Φ(1.54).$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.54) & =P(Z\le 1.54) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -1.54) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.54) \\  & =1-0.0618 \\  & =0.9382\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.54<Z<1.54) & =Φ(1.54)-Φ(-1.54) \\  & =0.9382-0.0618 \\  & =0.8764.\end{aligned}
$$
